chapter: Algiers parades and the wider city
title: White string bands and tailgate wagon band battles
summary: He saw white dance bands; bands advertised dances on wagons and backed tailgates together to 'buck' each other.

story.theme_name: Playing for dancers: dance bands and the dances themselves
story.community_name: Dancing to the band: quadrilles, waltzes and dance sets

blocks.x: Did you ever see any white dance band? Oh, yeah. In those days.

Oh, yeah. They did that? Yeah, yeah. String band, two, six pieces. Yeah, I saw plenty of them. We had them. During the time, I picked up here there, the young bunch around there, I mean they could play. I forget all the names now. One of them, daddy had a Jewish stuff. They all did now. We used to get in those, you know, used to have those furniture wagons. We used to get in there. We used to hook together, you know, tailgate. Yeah. You know about the bruners? Yeah, the bruners. Well, there's one over here. Well, he was playing, one of them was playing trumpet. Uh-huh. And we used to tie tailgate chains, you know, tie them together. Uh-huh. And Buckingham's one that sit there for hours.
I like the color. That's right.

Very good. Yeah. We buck like that. Well, during that time, all in the city, we used to meet like that. See, well, uh, used to give a lot of dances over there during that time. And you'd take, oh, you turn around, they had bands. You see, for that Sunday, the dance was going to be that Sunday night. Well, all the bands get out in the truck and advertise for the band. And we used to meet them like that. And we used to meet them like that. And where you turn, you see bands, backed up to one another, bucking. See, that for now, we're like that. Bucking like that. That's how they call that song that's tailgate around. Yeah. Yeah.
